d: CylindricalConstraint allows its attachments to slide along one axis and rotate about another axis, with optional assigned angular and/or linear power.
h:
For an overview on creating, visualizing, and simulating mechanical constraints, including CylindricalConstraint, see Mechanical constraints. Also see Roblox units to understand how Roblox units compare to metric units.

A CylindricalConstraint allows its attachments to slide along one axis and rotate about another axis. This constraint, along with a SpringConstraint, is ideal for building vehicle suspensions where the wheel shock can slide up and down while the wheel itself spins. This constraint can also be powered in both an angular and linear manner.

Orientation of the attachments affects how the cylindrical aspect will rotate. To ensure rotation occurs around the desired axis, each attachment's Axis and SecondaryAxis, visualized by the yellow and orange arrows, should point in the same direction.

Angular power

If a cylindrical's AngularActuatorType is set to Motor, it attempts to rotate the attachments with the goal of reaching its AngularVelocity. You can further control this rotation through both MotorMaxAngularAcceleration and MotorMaxTorque.

If a cylindrical's AngularActuatorType is set to Servo, it attempts to rotate to an angle specified by TargetAngle. This rotation is controlled by AngularSpeed, AngularResponsiveness, and ServoMaxTorque.

Linear power

If a cylindrical's ActuatorType is set to Motor, it attempts to translate the attachments with the goal of reaching Velocity. You can further control this translation through both MotorMaxAcceleration and MotorMaxForce.

If a cylindrical's ActuatorType is set to Servo, it attempts to translate the attachments to a set separation specified by TargetPosition. This translation is controlled by Speed, LinearResponsiveness, and ServoMaxForce.

Limits

You can set limits to restrict both the sliding range and rotation of a cylindrical constraint.

Enabling the LimitsEnabled property exposes the LowerLimit and UpperLimit values, as well as Restitution which defines the elasticity of the attachments when they reach either limit.

Enabling the AngularLimitsEnabled property exposes the LowerAngle and UpperAngle limits, as well as AngularRestitution which defines the elasticity of the attachments when they reach either limit.

Inclination angle

InclinationAngle defines the direction of the rotation axis as an angle from the X axis in the X/Y plane of Attachment0, from -180 to 180. This lets you tilt the rotating element without changing the sliding axis.

kid.simple: A CylindricalConstraint lets a part slide along one line and also spin around a line, both at the same time. That makes it perfect for car suspension, where a wheel spins and also bounces up and down over bumps. It can be powered for spinning, for sliding, or both, and both kinds of movement can have limits.
kid.analogy: Imagine a bead on a pencil. You can slide the bead up and down the pencil, and you can also spin it around the pencil.
keyPoints: A cylindrical constraint allows sliding along one axis and rotating around an axis.
Paired with a SpringConstraint, it makes vehicle suspension: the spring handles bounce, and the cylindrical lets the wheel spin and move up and down.
Point both attachments' yellow Axis and orange SecondaryAxis arrows the same way.
Spin power: `AngularActuatorType` Motor (goes for `AngularVelocity`, limited by `MotorMaxTorque`) or Servo (goes to `TargetAngle`).
Slide power: `ActuatorType` Motor (goes for `Velocity`, limited by `MotorMaxForce`) or Servo (goes to `TargetPosition`).
`LimitsEnabled` limits sliding with `LowerLimit` and `UpperLimit`. `AngularLimitsEnabled` limits spinning with `LowerAngle` and `UpperAngle`.
`InclinationAngle` (from -180 to 180) tilts the spin axis without changing the slide direction.

terms.attachment: A Roblox object you put inside a part to mark one exact point on it. Its Position is measured from the part's center, so an attachment at (-2, 0, 0) sits 2 studs toward the part's own left side.
terms.Axis / SecondaryAxis: Every attachment has its own arrows. `Axis` (yellow arrow) is its main X direction and `SecondaryAxis` (orange arrow) is its Y direction. With Orientation (0, 0, 0) the yellow arrow points along the part's X; with Orientation (0, 0, 90) it is turned a quarter turn to point straight up.
terms.suspension: The springy parts of a car that let wheels move up and down over bumps so the car body rides smoothly.
terms.angular vs linear: Angular is about spinning. Linear is about moving in a straight line.
terms.AngularVelocity: Spin speed in radians per second. 6.28 is about one full turn per second.
terms.TargetPosition: For a servo, how far apart along the slide line the attachments should be, in studs.
terms.LowerLimit / UpperLimit: The slide range in studs. -1 to 1 lets the part move 1 stud each way, 2 studs total.
terms.LowerAngle / UpperAngle: The spin range in degrees when angular limits are on.
terms.InclinationAngle: Tilts the spin axis away from the slide axis. At 0 they are the same line; at 90 the spin axis is sideways.
terms.restitution: How bouncy the stop is when a moving piece hits its limit. 0 means it stops dead, 1 means it bounces back as hard as it hit.

example.title: A spinning platform that can bob up and down
example.code:
local Workspace = game:GetService("Workspace")

local pole = Instance.new("Part")
pole.Size = Vector3.new(1, 10, 1)
pole.Position = Vector3.new(0, 5, -30)
pole.Anchored = true
pole.CanCollide = false
pole.Parent = Workspace

local platform = Instance.new("Part")
platform.Shape = Enum.PartType.Cylinder
platform.Size = Vector3.new(1, 12, 12)       -- a cylinder's length is along X
platform.Orientation = Vector3.new(0, 0, 90)  -- stand it up like a disc lying flat
platform.Position = Vector3.new(0, 5, -30)
platform.Parent = Workspace

-- Attachments with their Axis pointing straight up: slide up/down AND spin around up
local poleAtt = Instance.new("Attachment")
poleAtt.Orientation = Vector3.new(0, 0, 90)
poleAtt.Parent = pole

-- The platform is already turned (0, 0, 90), so its own X axis already points up.
-- A plain attachment at its center lines up with the pole's attachment.
local platformAtt = Instance.new("Attachment")
platformAtt.Parent = platform

local joint = Instance.new("CylindricalConstraint")
joint.Attachment0 = poleAtt
joint.Attachment1 = platformAtt

-- Spinning: motor at 1 radian per second (one turn about every 6.3 seconds)
joint.AngularActuatorType = Enum.ActuatorType.Motor
joint.AngularVelocity = 1
joint.MotorMaxTorque = 100000

-- Sliding: no motor, but it may only move between 1 stud below and 1 stud above
joint.LimitsEnabled = true
joint.LowerLimit = -1
joint.UpperLimit = 1
joint.Parent = pole
explain: The pole is anchored. The platform is a flat disc centered on the pole.

Both attachments' yellow Axis arrows point straight up: the pole's because we turned it (0, 0, 90), and the platform's because the whole platform is already turned (0, 0, 90). So the platform can slide up and down the pole and also spin around it.
The angular motor spins it at 1 radian per second. A full turn is about 6.28 radians, so one spin takes about 6.3 seconds.
Slide limits of -1 to 1 let the platform move 1 stud down or 1 stud up from the pole's center. Gravity pulls it to the -1 limit, and a player jumping on it can make it bob.
`MotorMaxTorque` starts at 0, so we give it a big number or the platform would not spin.

watchOut: If the part spins around the wrong line, check both Axis (yellow) and SecondaryAxis (orange) arrows on both attachments.
There are two separate actuators: `AngularActuatorType` for spinning and `ActuatorType` for sliding. Setting one does not power the other.
Without a spring, a suspension just drops to its lower limit. Add a SpringConstraint between the same two parts for real bounce.
